newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec voters do not want quick secession - poll.
newsitem.headline: Quebec voters do not want quick secession - poll.

text.p: The vast majority of Quebec voters do not want a quick rupture with Canada if the province votes in favor of secession in another referendum, according to a poll published on Monday.

The Southam News-COMPAS survey revealed that anywhere from 67 to 79 percent of respondents, depending on the margin of a vote in favor of secession, did not advocate a unilateral declaration of independence by the province, the Montreal Gazette newspaper said.
The poll also showed that 55 percent would accept a ruling by the Supreme Court of Canada that a unilateral declaration of independence violated Canada's constitution.
The telephone survey conducted May 1-7 also showed that overall support for Quebec independence had slipped, the Gazette said.
The share of Quebec voters approving the independence option dropped to 47 percent from a peak of 55 percent in December 1995, and 51 percent in February 1996.
The Bloc Quebecois, a separatist party that sits in the Canadian parliament, is seeking to maintain its official opposition status in the June 2 federal election.
In the 1993 election, the Bloc Quebecois won 54 of Quebec's 75 seats.
The poll asked respondents a harder question than the one posed in the October 1995 referendum. They were asked if they "want Quebec to separate from Canada and become an independent country."
COMPAS has posed that question to Quebec voters periodically over the past three years, the Gazette said.
The poll results were drawn from a survey of 600 voters in Quebec. Responses were considered accurate within 4.1 percentage points 19 times out of 20.

The poll was published on the same day that former Quebec Premier Jacques Parizeau was to release his controversial memoirs, in which he described how conditions were ripe for an immediate declaration of independence if separatists had won the October 1995 referendum.
Quebec separatists lost that referendum 49.4 percent to 50.6 percent.
